title: Editing a settings dropdown fires a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' alert on a completely idle app, and the alert text contradicts itself
summary: Confirmed real and NOT yet fixed — both cited files are clean in git (no pending edits). The cause is wholly inside skotiq_core, outside my ownership list, and nothing in the settings widget I do own can address it without being a disclosure-only patch. (a) weather_safety_provider.dart:879 — _enforceSafetyActions only declines to run SafeRig when none of shouldPause/shouldPark/shouldCloseDome is set. It never asks whether there is anything to safe, so enabling weather safety with no weather source resolves fail-closed to unsafe + shouldPark and genuinely executes the safing routine on an idle, disconnected app (which is why the verifier's log shows 'Secondary rig stopped'). (b) safe_rig_service.dart:498 sets detail='no action was possible' when no step ran, and :504 still interpolates it into 'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: $detail.$gap' — asserting the rig was safed and that nothing
needs_shared_change: TWO edits, both in skotiq_core. (1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/weather_safety_provider.dart, _enforceSafetyActions: extend the early return at line 879 so SafeRig is also skipped (returning true so the episode latches and does not retry every 5 minutes) when there is nothing to safe — i.e. sequenceExecutionStateProvider is not pausable AND mountStateProvider / domeStateProvider / cover / cameraStateProvider are all disconnected. The correct disclosure for that state already exists at lines 763-774 (the warning-severity failModeWarning toast, 'No weather data sources available'), so gating the escalation leaves the operator informed without a red CRITICAL and does not need new copy. (2) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/safe_rig_service.dart, _emitNotification lines 494-507: when steps.isEmpty, stop emitting 'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: no action was possible.' — emit showWarning with 'Nothing to safe: no run was active and no mount, dome or cover is connected.' preserving the existing mountAbsent gap sentence. Keep showError/CRITICAL for result.hasFailures and for the case where steps actually ran. Suggested test: a container with no connected devices and an idle sequencer, flip weatherSafetyEnabled true with no weather source, assert uiNotificationProvider got a warning and NOT an error titled 'Safe the rig', and that safeRigServiceProvider.safeTh

title: Sequence checkpoints and logs are written to the platform app-support directory, ignoring the configured data directory
summary: Independently confirmed the verifier's corrected location, not the reporter's ('the native bridge startup path'). Both writes are Dart and both bypass SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 calls backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir(supportDir.path) using getApplicationSupportDirectory(), and apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60-68 builds logDir from the same call. configureSkotiqDataDirectory (desktop_logging_init.dart:31-37) only FILLS SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when it is unset and is never consulted by either path, so an operator-supplied data dir is silently ignored and a GUI plus a headless daemon on one host share one skotiq_session.checkpoint. Both files are outside my ownership list (settings widgets only) and are plausibly being edited by concurrent agents, so I made no change rather than risk a conflicting edit.
needs_shared_change: Add one resolver next to configureSkotiqDataDirectory - e.g. `Future<Directory> resolveSkotiqDataRoot()` returning Platform.environment['SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR'] when non-empty and getApplicationSupportDirectory() otherwise - and use it in BOTH apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60 (logDir = <root>/logs) and packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 (sequencerSetCheckpointDir(<root>)). It must read Platform.environment directly rather than caching whatever _setProcessEnvironment wrote, so the operator-supplied value wins in both call orders.

title: Connection troubleshooter says it 'couldn't pin down the exact cause' while holding an error that names the exact cause, then gives four irrelevant hardware steps
summary: Confirmed real, and the verifier's location correction is right: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/troubleshooter/connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart is a pure renderer — it calls diagnoseConnectionFailure in initState and paints whatever comes back. Every part of the defect lives in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart, which is OUTSIDE my ownership (packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/**), so I did not edit it. I traced the classification against the source: the built-in guider preflight emits five first-party configuration errors from native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/builtin_guider.rs (:1265 'requires a connected camera in the active profile', :1276 '...connected mount...', :1306 'requires an active profile with a guide focal length', :1320 'requires positive camera pixel dimensions', :1329 'requires positive guide focal length and c
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart. (1) Add the built-in-guider preflight strings to _configurationMarkers (:263-274) — discriminating substrings are 'guide focal length', 'pixel size', 'positive camera pixel dimensions', 'requires an active profile', 'requires a connected camera/mount in the active profile' — so they classify as DiagnosticCategory.configuration instead of unknown. (2) _configurationSteps (:686-734) branches only on ascom / alpaca+indi; give the native/simulator branch a step naming the actual remedy ('Open Equipment > Edit Profile and set the guide scope focal length in mm'). (3) _unknownSteps (:736-769) must not emit 'Check the <device> is connected and powered / Reseat the cable, confirm power' for a device with no cable and no power — gate that step on a physical device. A jump-to-profile-editor button in connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart (which I do own) is pointless until the classifier stops answering 'unknown'.

title: The NIGHT STORY timeline (and every narrator detail sheet) is hidden whenever the session has no science products, even when narrator events exist
summary: Confirmed real by reading the current source, and the verifier's line-drift correction is right. The defect is in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_tab.dart — OUTSIDE my ownership (packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/**) and inside the concurrently-running r-analytics agent's area — so I did not edit it. Current tree: the allEmpty predicate at :472-482 tests ten SCIENCE product collections (lightCurve, transparency, transparencyRows, calibrations, psfTiles, residuals, moving, lineRatios, frameMetrics, tileMetrics) and never looks at the narrator feed; its early-return branch at :488-536 renders the session bar, ScienceStatusBanner, ScienceSolveRateCard, ScienceLadderCard and ScienceEmptyOnramp and then returns — so the NIGHT STORY heading plus NightStoryTimeline(sessionId: activeSessionId) at :687-693 is unreachable, and with it every narrator detail
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_tab.dart — render the NIGHT STORY section inside the `if (allEmpty)` branch (:488-536), between ScienceSolveRateCard and ScienceLadderCard, as `_SectionHeading(colors: colors, label: 'NIGHT STORY', icon: LucideIcons.bookOpen)` + `NightStoryTimeline(sessionId: activeSessionId)`. Rendering it unconditionally beats widening allEmpty with narratorFeedProvider, because the narrator is a session-narrative surface and not a science product — the user it was written for (imaged all night, no plate solver) is exactly the user allEmpty is true for. Test: seed imaging_sessions + captured_images + narrator_events with every science table empty and assert the NIGHT STORY heading renders.

title: Frames captured under a named target are reported as 'Untargeted', and the run's target breakdown is keyed by the SEQUENCE name instead of the target name
summary: Found and fixed the cause, which was one level below the finding. ExecutorEvent::TargetStarted has a bridge mapping (bridge/src/api/sequencer.rs:677 -> SequencerEvent::TargetChanged) and a Dart handler ('TargetStarted'/'TargetChanged' in event_operations.dart), but it had ZERO producers anywhere in the sequencer crate - the variant was declared at executor/mod.rs:1270 and never constructed. So SequenceProgress.currentTarget was null on every run ever executed, and stats_json.targetBreakdown fell through its documented fallback chain (progress.currentTarget ?? currentSequence.name ?? 'Sequence') to the SEQUENCE name. The executor now builds target_node_metadata from the SequenceDefinition at start (TargetHeader + TargetGroup, keyed by node id) and emits TargetStarted from the same one-shot node-entry branch that emits NodeStarted, plus TargetCompleted on Success only. A target with an emp
needs_shared_change: The Session Report's Targets section still prints 'Untargeted' because it groups on captured_images.target_id, which is honestly NULL when the TargetHeader carries no catalogTargetId (frame_attribution.dart is right to leave it null - inventing a catalog FK would be worse). Owner of packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/session_report_dialog.dart should group and label from the enclosing TargetHeader name (available in sequence_runs.sequence_snapshot_json) rather than from the catalog foreign key.

title: Four surfaces disagree about which filter a frame was taken through: filename says 'nofilter', DB says 'R', FITS header has no FILTER card, run stats say 'Unknown'
summary: Closed the surface inside my ownership, and it was a genuine two-resolvers-for-one-frame bug rather than a display issue. _registerSequenceFrame resolved the filter as `progress.currentFilter ?? filterWheelState.currentFilterName` and wrote 'R' to captured_images; _recordRunFrame, called from the same ExposureCompleted event, read `event.data['filter']` - a field SequencerEvent::ExposureCompleted does not carry at all (only ExposureStarted has it) - and therefore filed every frame under 'Unknown'. One frame, two answers, both persisted. There is now a single _resolveActiveFilter() that both call, so captured_images.filter and stats_json.targetBreakdown cannot diverge again. 'Unknown' is still the bucket when nothing can name the filter - that is the honest answer, not a fallback.
needs_shared_change: The 'nofilter' filename token and the missing FITS FILTER card are produced natively in native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/node/instructions/expose.rs and instructions.rs (not owned). IMPORTANT: that half looks already in flight in this working tree - expose.rs carries 73 uncommitted added lines including resolve_burst_filter(), which falls back to observed_wheel_filter() exactly as this finding asks. Whoever owns it should confirm the resolved name reaches BOTH the save-path renderer and FrameContext.filter_name: instructions.rs:3534 still reads only `config.filter.clone().or_else(|| ctx.current_filter.clone())`, with no wheel fallback.

title: Pre-flight warns that a step is scheduled 'before target rises' when it is scheduled AFTER the rise time it prints
summary: Real, and the verifier's re-location is correct - I confirmed it myself rather than taking it on trust. The comparison and the literal live in SequenceTimeEstimator.findTimingConflicts (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart:786-798): it warns on a bare `timing.estimatedStart.isBefore(window.riseTime!)` against a single rise instant instead of against the visibility interval containing the scheduled time, and _formatTime (line 411) prints HH:mm with no date, so a rise on the next calendar day reads as one that already passed. Both files are outside my ownership list (services/, not providers/sequence/sequence_executor/), so I did not edit them.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart: findTimingConflicts must test membership of the rise/set interval that CONTAINS the scheduled instant (a target up between rise and set produces no warning at all), and when it does warn it must name the boundary actually violated, printed with a date whenever it is not the same calendar day as the scheduled time.

title: Pre-flight dark-library check uses the camera default temperature (-10C), not the temperature the sequence's Cool Camera node will actually reach (15C)
summary: Real and unconditional, confirmed by reading the code at the verifier's location: preflight_rules.dart:116-118 does `final cameraState = ref.read(cameraStateProvider); final camTargetTemp = cameraState.targetTemp;` and stamps that onto every DarkFrameRequirement at line 139. Nothing in that rule consults the sequence's CoolCameraNode, so the dark match - and the 'Capture missing darks' action it offers - use a temperature the run never reaches. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart is a sibling of my ownership root (providers/sequence/rules/, not providers/sequence/sequence_executor/), so I did not edit it.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart: resolve the planned sensor temperature by walking the sequence for the cooling instruction that precedes each exposure node and using its setpoint; fall back to the camera's current setpoint only when no Cool Camera node precedes the exposures, and say which temperature was assumed in the message.

title: The top-bar run chip still reads 'Sequence Running' (green) while the sequence is paused
summary: Confirmed at the finding's own location: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/sequencer_screen_parts/tab_bar.dart:112 hard-codes the literal 'Sequence Running' styled with colors.success, and the widget has no paused variant at all - so the chip contradicts the toolbar chip one row away and the node's own PAUSED badge. Outside my ownership (skotiq_app screens).
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/sequencer_screen_parts/tab_bar.dart: drive the chip from sequenceExecutionStateProvider - the same SequenceExecutionState enum the toolbar chip uses - instead of a boolean isRunning, and give it paused (amber), recovering and stopping variants so two indicators one row apart cannot disagree about whether the rig is exposing.

title: sequence_runs.status stays 'running' while the run is paused, so any non-GUI consumer thinks the rig is still exposing
summary: Confirmed structurally, not just observationally. The Dart half of this fix is in a file I own - the 'Paused' and 'Resumed' cases in event_operations.dart already run on every pause/resume - but there is nothing for them to call: SequenceRunsDao (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/sequence_runs_dao.dart) exposes startRun, finishRun (which also stamps ended_at, so it cannot be reused for a mid-run pause), updateStats and read-only queries, and no method that can change status alone. The DAO is outside my ownership, so this is one shared line away from done.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/sequence_runs_dao.dart: add `Future<void> markRunStatus(int runId, String status)` that writes ONLY the status column and never touches ended_at. Once it exists, the two calls are `_ref.read(sequenceRunsDaoProvider).markRunStatus(runId, 'paused')` in the 'Paused' case and `...'running'` in the 'Resumed' case of event_operations.dart, guarded on currentRunIdProvider being non-null. The _statsSealed guard deliberately does not apply - this is a status write, not a stats write - but the call must be skipped once _runFinalized is true so it cannot resurrect a finished run.

title: The Continue Session handoff dialog says 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' while naming the sequence in its own header and with a real profile active
summary: Confirmed at both the display site and the upstream cause the verifier identified, and neither is mine. The strings come from quick_start_dialog.dart:184-185 ('profileName ?? Unknown Profile' / 'sequenceName ?? No Sequence'). The reason those nulls exist is that imaging_sessions rows are written with profile_id and sequence_id NULL, and QuickStartService builds its context from imaging_sessions (quick_start_service.dart:624). The writer is SessionStateNotifier.startSession, called from packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor.dart:623 with targetName/targetRa/targetDec only - and that file is a sibling of, not inside, the sequence_executor/ directory I own.
needs_shared_change: Two coordinated edits, neither in my files: (1) SessionStateNotifier.startSession must accept and persist profileId + sequenceId (and the equipment snapshot); (2) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor.dart:623 must pass the active equipment profile's id and sequence.databaseId - both are already in hand at that call site. Changing only the fallback strings in quick_start_dialog.dart would replace one false claim with another.

title: Continue Session dialog dates yesterday's session as 'Today at 14:57'
summary: Confirmed verbatim by reading the code: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116 _formatDate does `final diff = now.difference(dt); if (diff.inDays == 0) return 'Today at ...'` - it compares ELAPSED duration, not calendar day. So every session under 24h old is labelled Today no matter which day it happened, and 'Yesterday' can only ever appear for sessions 24-48h old. Outside my ownership (skotiq_app widgets).
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart: compare calendar days, e.g. `DateUtils.dateOnly(now).difference(DateUtils.dateOnly(dt)).inDays`, and fall through to an explicit date beyond a week. The same _formatDate bug will be in any sibling that copied it - worth grepping for 'Today at ' before landing.

title: 'Load Previous Setup' is inert: it restores no equipment, no sequence and writes nothing to the log - it just closes the dialog
summary: Real, and the verifier's correction matters: it is not silent, it shows a green 'Loaded previous setup for previous target from frame 1' snackbar - a false-success claim, which changes the fix. Confirmed the mechanism at quick_start_checker.dart:_handleStartFresh (~line 244): every restore step is gated on context.profileId / context.sequenceId / the equipment snapshot being non-null, and all three are NULL for the same upstream reason as the 'Unknown Profile' finding (imaging_sessions is written without them). Both files are outside my ownership.
needs_shared_change: Same owner as the 'Unknown Profile' finding, two parts: (1) stamp profile_id / sequence_id / equipment_snapshot onto imaging_sessions at run start so there is genuinely something to restore; (2) packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_checker.dart must not emit the success snackbar unless something was actually restored, and quick_start_dialog.dart should disable/relabel the primary action when the context does not resolve - the dialog already knows, since it is printing 'Unknown Profile' / 'No Sequence' two lines above the button.

title: Builder and Pre-Flight disagree about how long the same sequence takes: '~18m 54s' vs 'Duration 27m'
summary: Confirmed as two independent estimators rather than one dialog bug, exactly as the verifier re-located it. The Builder chip and timeline go through SequenceTimeEstimator (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart, called from screens/sequencer/widgets/node_timing_section.dart and sequence_timeline.dart); the Pre-Flight Simulation panel calls `const PreSessionSimulator().simulate(...)` at preflight_validation_dialog.dart:134 and renders it at :735. Two engines, so the two numbers have no reason to agree. Both files are outside my ownership.
needs_shared_change: Collapse to one engine rather than reconciling two: either have the Pre-Flight Simulation panel render SequenceTimeEstimator's result, or have SequenceTimeEstimator delegate to PreSessionSimulator. Whichever survives, show the SAME per-node breakdown on both surfaces so a remaining difference (slew/settle overheads the builder does not model) is attributable instead of two bare totals. Worth also checking the finding's secondary claim while in there - the Builder bills a Cool Camera node its configured Max Duration, which is why the header estimate did not move when the setpoint changed from -10C to +15C.

title: Every node failure is listed twice in the Session Report and raised as two identical toasts
summary: There are TWO independent multipliers. (a) FIXED -- the node-runtime retry loop. `is_device_disconnected_message` (instructions.rs:278) classifies 'No dome connected' as a disconnect, so `execute_instruction_with_disconnect_retry` re-ran the node once per recovery cycle, and EVERY execution published its own `ExecutorEvent::InstructionFailed` from `log_and_get_status_with_context`. Dart turns each into one session-report error line plus one Critical toast (event_operations.dart:205 `_recordRunError`) -- exactly the reporter's '6 identical lines' for one failed Open Dome node, which I reproduced as 6 in a test. The failure is now published on the first execution only: the retry wrapper scopes a task-local `DISCONNECT_RETRY_ATTEMPT` around `instruction.execute`, and the publish site skips when it is a retry. First-attempt rather than last is deliberate: no path (no recovery driver, recover
needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/sequencer.rs:420 `api_sequencer_subscribe_events` must be idempotent -- guard its two `spawn_supervised_restart` calls behind a `static SUBSCRIBED: AtomicBool` / OnceCell so repeated calls are no-ops; OR make packages/skotiq_bridge/lib/src/bridge_stub/sequencer_operations.dart:623 subscribe once per process instead of on every `sequencerStart()`. Prefer the Rust-side guard -- it also covers the headless and remote entry points. Note `spawn_supervised_restart` (bridge/src/util/supervisor.rs) is a bare tokio::spawn with no registry, so the task name does NOT dedupe. Worth checking whether the same duplication is inflating frame events / captured_images rows too.

title: Sequence header reports '0 frames / 0m' for a Science Photometry node that says '60 frames', and pre-flight claims 'No exposure nodes found'
summary: Confirmed as the verifier diagnosed, and entirely in Dart -- nothing in native/skotiq_native/sequencer participates. The two liars are `Sequence._countExposures` at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart:168 (walks the tree adding only ExposureNode and SmartExposureNode) and `NoExposuresRule.validate` at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/exposure_rules.dart:152 (`sequence.nodes.values.any((n) => (n is ExposureNode && n.isEnabled) || (n is SmartExposureNode && n.isEnabled && n.plans.isNotEmpty))`). Neither knows SciencePhotometryNode exists. The verifier's correction stands: the duration half is already implemented in SequenceTimeEstimator, so only the frame count and the rule are wrong. The Rust node (node/instructions/science_photometry.rs) captures `config.count` frames correctly -- the run is right, the planning
needs_shared_change: 1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart:168 `_countExposures` -- add a SciencePhotometryNode arm returning `mult * node.count` alongside the ExposureNode / SmartExposureNode arms. 2) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/exposure_rules.dart:152 `NoExposuresRule` -- add `|| (n is SciencePhotometryNode && n.isEnabled)` to the `hasEnabledExposure` predicate so a photometry-only sequence is not told it will capture no images.

title: The Collapse button blanks the whole sequence tree to an empty grey rectangle
summary: Pure Flutter widget defect with no native/sequencer involvement -- the tree is rendered entirely from the Dart Sequence model; Rust is never consulted for layout. Reproduced by both reporter and verifier. The verifier's refinement is the useful lead: rows ABOVE the collapsed region still render, the button is inert on a sequence with no Target node, and a Target card is required to reproduce -- which points at the collapsed-state builder mishandling the Target-header subtree (emitting an empty/zero-height child instead of one collapsed row per top-level node) rather than at the collapse toggle itself.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree/node_tree_view.dart (collapsed-state builder) -- when collapsed, emit one collapsed row per top-level node INCLUDING the Target card instead of an empty container. Guard it with a widget test that builds [Target(+children), Slew, SmartExposure], toggles Collapse and asserts the collapsed-row finder has the top-level count; a golden would not have caught a solid grey block either.

title: Pre-flight warns 'Slew to Target scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41'
summary: Confirmed and located, but it is Dart. The warning is built at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart:791 ('before target rises at ${_formatTime(window.riseTime!)}'), and the comparison that guards it is clock-time-only with no date -- which is why a target that rose at 03:41 and is at the zenith at 12:47 is reported as not yet risen. Nothing in native/skotiq_native/sequencer computes this warning; the Rust visibility code in scheduling/ is a separate run-time path that pre-flight does not use. The app's own target card on the same screen computes Alt 77.8 deg from the same coordinates, so the contradiction is internal to the Dart layer.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart around :791 -- compare full DateTimes on the observing night, not times-of-day. The rise/transit/set triple for a night wraps midnight, so the correct test is whether the node's scheduled instant falls inside the [rise, set] interval anchored to that night's date; a target whose rise time is earlier the same day is UP, not 'not yet risen'. Add a regression test with RA 6h30m / Dec +40 at lat 40 scheduled near local noon asserting NO conflict is raised.

title: A rig with no filter wheel cannot create any integration goal, so the autopilot can never be given a target
summary: Confirmed at the reported location. /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq2/packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/scheduler/widgets/integration_goals_editor.dart short-circuited the whole _AddGoalRow on `widget.availableFilters.isEmpty` with a warning telling the operator to configure a filter wheel. Fixed: a rig with no named filters now gets exactly one selectable slot carrying `smartNightUnfilteredName` (the empty string — the same wire contract Smart Night's wheel-less path plans against, per plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart:85-98), rendered as 'No filter' in both the dropdown and the existing-goal rows (the sentinel used to render as a blank cell). The hard refusal survives only for the real fault the Smart Night builder already distinguishes: a wheel that IS connected and still reports zero slots. The wheel provider is watched only inside that branch — watching it unconditionally pul
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/scheduler/scheduler_engine.dart:787-801 gates a goal on `c.availableFilters` containing its name (and again at :1071-1085 and :1119-1130), so an unfiltered goal on a wheel-less rig (availableFilters == []) is still rejected with 'required filter(s) not in equipment wheel ()'. The one-line fix is in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:552-563: have SchedulerCandidateLoader._availableFilters return smartNightPlanningFilters(profile.filterNames) instead of profile.filterNames, so a wheel-less profile yields [''] and every containment check plus buildSequenceForCandidate works unchanged.

title: False "Rises late" warning on a target that is up all night, and the same card gives two different rise times
summary: Diagnosis confirmed by source reading; no fix made, because both producers sit outside this agent's ownership. Chain: TargetSuggestionService (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/target_suggestion_service.dart:145) -> TargetScoringService.scoreTargetForNight (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/target_scoring.dart:318) -> _generateNightWarnings, whose 'Rises late' block at :1004-1024 fires purely off `visibility.riseTime`. That visibility is the nightMid-anchored solve at target_scoring.dart:403-412, and calculateObjectVisibility (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:1096-1107) anchors its 24-hour search at `DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12)` — LOCAL NOON. A nightMid of ~01:30 on Aug 2 therefore searches Aug 2 12:00 -> Aug 3 12:00 and reports a rise a full day later, in daylight (11:54). The card's chart footer is a
needs_shared_change: TWO files, both outside the ownership list. (1) packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/target_scoring.dart: scoreTargetForNight already walks every 15-minute sample from nightStart to nightEnd against the skyline-aware effective minimum (:337-387). Record the first sample time that clears that minimum (null when it never does), pass it into _generateNightWarnings, and gate 'Rises late' on THAT rather than visibility.riseTime — dropping the warning outright when the first sample (nightStart) already clears the minimum, which is exactly M92's case at >80 deg when astronomical dark begins. Expose the same value on VisibilityInfo so there is one rise time per card. (2) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart:155-163 must stop solving rise/transit/set independently: give AltitudeChart an optional injected ObjectVisibility and have the planner cards pass suggestion.visibility.

title: Observing Alerts refresh is a silent no-op and the screen can never show anything
summary: Added a per-source status strip under the header of /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq2/packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/transients_screen.dart: a spinner plus 'Checking sources…' while a fetch is in flight, then one entry per enabled fetchable source — 'AAVSO: 0 alerts' (counted from the returned alerts by TransientAlert.source), 'TNS: skipped — no API key' when the bot id/name or the SecretField.tnsApiKey secret is missing, 'AAVSO: failed' on the error path, 'No alert source is enabled' when none is — and a 'checked HH:MM' / 'never checked' stamp. The stamp is driven by a ref.listen on activeTransientAlertsProvider rather than by the refresh button, so the 15-minute poll updates it too. The operator can now tell a quiet sky from a fetch that never ran or never could.
needs_shared_change: TWO core changes remain, both in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transient_alert_service.dart. (1) :80-81 `_aavsoApiUrl` is 'https://www.aavso.org/vsx/index.php?view=api.list&format=json&maxrec=50', which 301-redirects to vsx.aavso.org and then returns exactly {"VSXObjects":[]} — api.list with no selector returns an empty set by design, so the only implemented broadband source is empty by construction. It needs the vsx.aavso.org host and a query that actually selects recent alerts. (2) getAllAlerts (:843-900) swallows PARTIAL failures into a logger.warning; the per-source _TransientFetchOutcome list should be returned alongside the alerts so the strip can print 'AAVSO: failed — <reason>' instead of only inferring failure from the total-failure exception.

title: Tutorial Tours run as a modal on whatever screen you are on and tell you to click tabs that are not there -- and the modal blocks every one of them
summary: Confirmed the cited locations by reading them: help_tutorials_settings.dart:179-183 wires onStart/onRestart straight to notifier.restartTutorial(TutorialCategory.equipmentSetup), and tutorial_provider.dart _restartTutorial only writes activeCategory/currentStepIndex — it never routes. The overlay is mounted by app_shell.dart over whatever screen is showing, so the steps ('Click the Profiles tab', 'Click the Connections tab') describe a screen the user is not on, behind a scrim that swallows the clicks that would take them there. Every file involved is outside my ownership list, and adding UI text about it would be the disclosure-only non-fix the brief forbids.
needs_shared_change: The machinery is already half-built: TutorialStep (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/tutorial/tutorial_models.dart) already carries targetKey, actionTarget, isInteractive and a spotlight shape, and the equipmentSetup steps set none of them. (1) Add a target route to TutorialStep and have tutorial_provider.dart's _restartTutorial/resumeTutorial push it before publishing step 0, so a tour opens the screen it describes. (2) Populate targetKey/isInteractive for the equipmentSetup + connection steps so packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/tutorial_overlay.dart spotlights the real control and lets taps outside the cutout reach the UI instead of rendering a centred modal card. (3) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/help_tutorials_settings.dart: the row still reads 'Not started' while a tour is running — bind its status to state.activeCategory.

title: Paired devices always say 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' -- last_connected_at is never written
summary: Confirmed the verifier's sharper diagnosis by reading the code: PairingDatabase.updateLastConnected exists (pairing_database.dart:138) and its only non-test caller is TokenManager.verifySessionToken (token_manager.dart:297), which the desktop HTTP auth path never calls — the server authenticates from its in-memory BoundedTokenGrantMap _pairedSessionTokens, so no request ever reaches the stamping code. The write has to happen where a bearer resolves, in files outside my ownership. Nothing in pairing_screen.dart can make the column true, and adding UI text about it would be disclosure, not a fix.
needs_shared_change: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart: where a bearer resolves against _pairedSessionTokens (~:1030), stamp last_connected_at for the matched deviceId, throttled to at most once per minute per device (a per-device DateTime map alongside the grant map), and do the same on the /events WebSocket upgrade. The write already exists — PairingDatabase.updateLastConnected(deviceId). Once written, packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/pairing_screen.dart already renders it (_deviceStatus / pairingLastConnected) with no further change; the row copy is already honest about the record vs the device.

title: 'Active Viewers' on the Remote Access page counts co-imaging collaborators, not connected remote clients -- it stays 0 with a live dashboard socket open
summary: The number is real, but it is not what the label said: WebServerState.activeViewers is mutated only by setActiveViewers, whose only non-test call site assigns collabState.viewers.length from the co-imaging collaboration manager. Nothing anywhere in the app publishes a connected-remote-client count, and producing one requires the headless API server's WS/SSE registry, which I do not own. Within ownership the row is now labelled 'Co-imaging viewers' — which is true — so the Remote Access page no longer answers 'is anyone connected?' with a number about something else. Marked partial rather than fixed on purpose: the operator still cannot see a connected-client count.
needs_shared_change: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/*: publish a live connected-client count (the /events WS + SSE registry size) into packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/web_server_provider.dart as a NEW field (e.g. connectedClients) — do NOT overload activeViewers, which packages/skotiq_app/lib/.../status_bar/session_sharing.dart reads for co-imaging. Then add a 'Connected clients' row next to the co-imaging one in remote_access_settings.dart. Also packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/skotiq_localizations/translations.dart remoteAccessDetailsBody still advertises this panel as the place to find 'viewer counts'.

title: Framing screen reports the wrong sensor size (1920x1080) for a camera that delivers 4144x2822
summary: Confirmed still present, and the verifier's correction holds: nothing in screens/framing is wrong. framing_provider/support.dart faithfully uses the geometry the camera ADVERTISES, and the simulated camera advertises SIM_W x SIM_H = 1920x1080 (api/devices/simulation.rs:73-74). The liar is the manual-capture generator at native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:824-825, which still hardcodes `let full_width = 4144 / bin_x; let full_height = 2822 / bin_y;` - so sim_frame.rs:36-42's claim that the three paths were unified is still false. Simulator-only; on real ASCOM/INDI hardware the delivered frame matches CameraXSize.
needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:824-825 - replace the hardcoded 4144/2822 with `crate::sim_frame::SIM_W as u32 / bin_x` and `SIM_H as u32 / bin_y`, matching what SimulatedCamera advertises and what the sequencer/autofocus path already generates. Add a Rust test asserting api_camera_get_last_image's width/height equal get_simulator_capabilities' sensor_width/height at every binning.

title: Abort capture does not actually stop the exposure - the camera runs the full duration after "Exposure cancelled"
summary: Fixed the half that is real on BOTH sim and real hardware: the UI kept counting down an exposure the operator had already cancelled ('97% / 1.0s remaining' four seconds after the cancel). ExposureProgress keeps ticking after a cancel because the native waiter publishes progress until the driver reports not-exposing or the duration deadline passes, so the ring narrated a frame that was never going to arrive. The preview now drops the determinate ring, the percentage and the '...s remaining' line the moment an abort is issued and shows an indeterminate 'Stopping exposure...'; the toolbar's abort X is withdrawn (a second abort has nothing left to cancel). `_isStoppingCapture` is prop-drilled from the imaging screen into both children - one source of truth, no mirrored provider. The Dart side already issues a real abort (ImagingService.cancelExposure resolves the pending completer, driving c
needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs, api_camera_cancel_exposure (~line 1230): the `sim_` branch only sets `camera.status.state = Idle` and logs 'Exposure cancelled' while the exposure future sleeps on to completion, whereas every real-device branch calls mark_camera_exposure_aborted + DeviceManager::camera_abort_exposure. The sim needs a real cancellation token that the exposure loop polls so a cancelled sim exposure actually ENDS. Until then the simulator fails in the pass-making direction and cannot validate abort at all.

title: The "1:1 zoom" button and the "100%" readout are fit-to-window - a 4144 px frame is shown at 987 screen px (23.8%)
summary: Root cause is that the preview carried TWO meanings of zoom. ImagingViewerState.zoomLevel is a multiplier relative to fit-to-window and ImageDisplayWidget honours that (CustomPaint sized constraints.constrain(imageSize), then BoxFit.contain). But the toolbar printed zoomLevel*100 as if it were screen-px-per-image-px, AND - not previously reported - every overlay painter was handed the same raw multiplier alongside computeImageOffset, whose `scaledSize = imageSize * zoomLevel` is native-scale arithmetic. Measured in a widget test: a 2000x1200 frame renders at 0.437 while the overlays were told 1.0, so star / annotation / catalog / celestial-grid / PSF / residual / uniformity / clip / moving-track markers and the arcsecond scale bar were spread over 2.3x (4.2x on the reported 4144 px sensor) their real footprint and landed on target only at the exact centre of the frame. New previewFitScal
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/imaging_viewer_state_provider.dart - the 1:1 button is still fit. zoom1to1() and fitToWindow() have byte-identical bodies (`zoomLevel: 1.0, panOffset: Offset.zero`) and the notifier exposes no way to set an arbitrary multiplier, so the screen cannot ask for zoomLevel = 1/fitScale. Needed: `void zoomToDisplayScale(double target, double fitScale) { state = state.copyWith(zoomLevel: (target / fitScale).clamp(minZoom, maxZoom), panOffset: Offset.zero); }`, plus lowering minZoom (0.25 today) so fit stays reachable for a big sensor in a small pane. The imaging screen then calls it with the fit scale derived from previewDisplayScaleProvider. Both consumers of that provider are files I own, so the core change is additive and low-risk - I left it out only because the file is outside my ownership list.

title: The autofocus result overlay never auto-dismisses and follows the user onto every other screen, covering controls
summary: Confirmed real, and the finding's `where` is wrong: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/focus_panel.dart contains nothing about this overlay. The real code is AutofocusProgressOverlay in packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay.dart, mounted once in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:769 - deliberately shell-mounted (documented in the widget header as the single live V-curve surface), which is exactly why it follows the user onto Guiding / Plan Tonight / Framing. AutofocusOverlayNotifier.onAutofocusCompleted (skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/autofocus_progress_provider.dart:225) sets isMinimized but leaves isVisible true with no timer, so the pill persists indefinitely. All three files are outside my ownership list.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/autofocus_progress_provider.dart - onAutofocusCompleted should arm a ~10 s Timer calling dismiss(), cancelled by any new run, by onAutofocusFailed and in dispose; a FAILED run should stay up because it carries an error the operator must read. AND packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay.dart + screens/shell/app_shell.dart:769 - keep the overlay shell-mounted while a run is IN PROGRESS, but gate the completed-result pill on the imaging route so it cannot cover the Guiding Tour card or the Framing rotation controls.

title: Selecting Spanish translates only the nav rail and Settings; every other screen stays English
summary: The picker no longer claims more than it does. The Spanish subtitle 'Elegir el idioma de la interfaz principal' (choose the language of the MAIN interface) is replaced with one stating the real scope (menus, navigation and Settings; other screens stay English), and the Spanish option now reads 'Español (beta)' so an unfinished translation cannot read as a finished one. The dropdown also carries language CODES with display labels, so the stored value no longer depends on comparing translated strings.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/skotiq_localizations/translations.dart: fix 'generalLanguageDesc' in the es block (:617) and add a key for the scope sentence now hardcoded in general_settings.dart. Beyond that, es coverage for dashboard/imaging/sequencer/status-bar is a product decision — finish it or drop the option.

title: Red night mode leaves the Moon phase disc near-white — a dark-adaptation flare on the default screen
summary: Confirmed in source and located exactly, but the owning file is outside this agent's ownership list. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/standby/moon_card.dart:51 passes `litColor: const Color(0xFFD6DCE2)` — RGB(214,220,226), the exact pixel the audit sampled — into _MoonPainter (:164-245), which fills the disc with `Paint()..color = litColor` (:188) regardless of theme. `litColor` has exactly one production caller.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/standby/moon_card.dart:51 — drive litColor (and the darkColor beside it) from the theme ramp (SkotiqColors.of(context).textPrimary / .surfaceAlt) so Red night maps the disc to dim red, plus a red-night widget test asserting the painted colour follows the theme.

title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them
summary: The picker now emits only values clockProvider can parse (UTC and UTC±HH:MM, 38 entries covering every standard world offset), so choosing one installs a real FixedOffsetClock; an IANA label left by the old picker is migrated once to its standard-time offset so a choice already made starts being honoured. The row gained a subtitle derived from clockProvider itself — it shows the live time the chosen offset produces, says 'Ignored while "Use system time" is on' when it is, and admits when a stored label cannot be applied — so the control can no longer be silently ignored without the screen contradicting itself.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/widgets/status_bar.dart:188/200/209 and the Dashboard header/twilight widgets must read clockProvider instead of DateTime.now(); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/clock_provider.dart:98-113 should log the fallback instead of silently returning SystemClock (its own comment claims it is logged).

title: The session checkpoint lives outside the database, so the app offers to resume a sequence its own database has never heard of — and the failure dialog contradicts itself
summary: First half is ALREADY FIXED in the working tree by an earlier wave: app_shell.dart:82-89 resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory anchors the checkpoint to the directory holding the OPEN DATABASE (with adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint at :106-135 migrating a legacy application-support file only when SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is unset), so a checkpoint can only be found beside the database whose run wrote it and the frame count can no longer describe another instance's night. Second half is still live and outside ownership: app_shell.dart:527-535 renders SkotiqAlert(title: 'Recovery did not complete', message: '$lastError\n\nThe checkpoint is still available…') where lastError (:148/:163) is the raw caught object, so 'Exception: No valid checkpoint to resume from' prints verbatim directly above a sentence asserting the checkpoint is still available.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:527-535 — replace the raw '$lastError' interpolation with a mapped message, and make the 'checkpoint is still available' sentence conditional on backend.hasCheckpoint()/getCheckpointInfo().canResume instead of asserting it unconditionally after a failure that may itself have been 'No valid checkpoint to resume from'.

title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead and only the selected network's blocker is explained
summary: Confirmed real and correctly located: transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 renders the three chips with `onTap: enabled ? … : null`, :142-151 renders _disabledReason ONLY for the selected _format, and skotiq_chip.dart:65-68 returns the bare chip when onTap is null — same fill, border and text colour as an enabled chip, no Semantics, no cursor change, so a disabled chip is indistinguishable and silently swallows the tap. I did NOT fix it: this is the SAME defect, in the same file and the same line range, as the r-analytics agent's finding 'Transient Discovery Report: the AAVSO and MPC network chips are inert…' (reports/coverage/fix2/r-analytics.json cites :129-141 and :142-148). Two agents editing that block concurrently would collide, and screens/analytics is theirs.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_panel.dart — duplicate of the r-analytics agent's assignment; let that agent land it. Their proposed fix (allow selecting a disabled network so its reason renders, or render a reason under every disabled chip) also closes this finding. One thing to ADD to their scope that only this finding surfaces: SkotiqChip itself gives a disabled chip no visual or semantic distinction (packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/components/skotiq_chip.dart:65-68), so 'looks disabled' needs a design-system change, not just a panel change — shared-widget territory.

title: Recovering a stale session stamps end_time = now, inflating its duration by days
summary: Confirmed present and unfixed. The verifier's correction is right: session_service.dart:431 is only the scan; the write is markSessionAborted (session_service.dart:538-545) -> ImagingRecordsRepository.endSession -> packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/sessions_dao.dart:108-115, whose body is `endTime: Value(DateTime.now())` with no way for a caller to say otherwise. Neither file is in my ownership list (I own only images_dao and science_dao), so I did not edit them. My session-elapsed work for the two duration findings does NOT paper over this: it only chooses an honest figure while end_time is NULL, and once recovery stamps `now` the row looks like a legitimately closed 60-hour session everywhere.
needs_shared_change: (1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/sessions_dao.dart:108 - `Future<void> endSession(int id, {String status = 'completed', DateTime? endTime})` writing `endTime: Value(endTime ?? DateTime.now())`. (2) Thread the same optional parameter through ImagingRecordsRepository.endSession (imaging_records_repository.dart:181). (3) session_service.dart markSessionAborted: close an abandoned session at its last frame, not at the clock - `final last = await _imagesDao.getLastCapturedAtForSession(sessionId); await _records.endSession(sessionId, status: 'aborted', endTime: (last != null && last.isAfter(session.startTime)) ? last : session.startTime);`. No such DAO method exists yet; the query is `SELECT MAX(captured_at) FROM captured_images WHERE session_id = ?`. I deliberately did NOT add it to images_dao.dart as dead code - add it in the same change that calls it. Test: seed a session with status='active', end_time NULL and frames ending two days ago, run the recovery path, assert end_time equals the last frame's captured_at, not now.

title: "Export report" produces a Science Report with no light curve and no period analysis
summary: Confirmed present and unfixed. buildMarkdown (science_report_exporter.dart:61-100) writes seven sections and never reads photometry_measurements at all - _photometrySnapshot (:168-206) is fed only getCalibrationsForSession(), so its no-data sentence 'No photometric calibration produced this session.' sits under a heading called '## Photometry' for a session with 80 measurements. The exporter is in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/ and is not mine. Note for the fixer: no new DAO method is needed - ScienceDao.getPhotometryForSession(sessionId) already exists at science_dao.dart:118 (that file IS mine and needs no change).
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/science_report_exporter.dart. (1) Rename the existing section to '## Photometric calibration' in both branches of _photometrySnapshot so its no-data sentence stops reading as 'you have no photometry'. (2) In buildMarkdown add `final photometry = await _scienceDao.getPhotometryForSession(sessionId);` and a `_lightCurveSnapshot(photometry)` section between _frameCounts and the calibration block: N points, first/last timestamp in UTC, the target object id (role == 'target'), the comparison ids, and mean/RMS differential magnitude. (3) Add a '## Period analysis' section. The period result is UI state (periodAnalysisProvider), not a stored product, so the exporter should take an optional `PeriodAnalysisResult? period` that the Science tab's Export button passes from ref.read(periodAnalysisProvider).result, printing LS best period + FAP + searched range and BLS period/depth/SDE when non-null, and 'Not run for this session.' when null - which is true, unlike today's silence.

title: BLS card gives no significance verdict, and its SDE scores pure noise higher than a strong periodic signal
summary: The ordering defect is real and is NOT fixed: I re-read period_analysis_service.dart:604-621 and the statistic is computed over the whole SR spectrum, peak included, so a coherent signal inflates its own baseline mean and std and deflates its own SDE. (I checked the one thing that would have been a cheap unit bug - srSpectrum[ip] is already sqrt'ed at :557 and peakSr is sqrt(globalBestSr) at :620, so the units DO match; the problem is the unmasked baseline, not a scale error.) That file is outside my ownership. What I did fix is the half that is mine: the BLS column printed a bare 'SDE: 3.1' with no threshold, so a user comparing two runs would rank 2.6 below 3.1. It now reads 'SDE: 3.1 (below the 6.0 significance threshold; compare SDE only within one light curve)'.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/period_analysis_service.dart:604-621. Exclude the peak's own neighbourhood from the baseline before computing mean/std - standard BLS-SDE practice: find peakIndex (the trial whose srSpectrum entry equals peakSr), build the baseline from trials whose period differs from globalBestPeriod by more than ~20% (or simply outside +/- nTrials/20 indices), compute srMean/srStd over that subset only, and fall back to the full spectrum when fewer than ~20 trials survive. Verify with the three controlled 80-point curves from the finding (pure noise; injected 20-min sinusoid amplitude 0.10 mag; injected box transit depth 0.150 mag at P=20 min): the ordering must become noise < sinusoid < transit and the transit must clear the 6.0 threshold the service's own doc comment at :81 states. Once it does, period_analysis_panel.dart:592-599's Strong/Noteworthy badge starts firing and the 'compare SDE only within one light curve' caveat I added can be dropped.

title: Diagnostics tab shows loading skeletons forever for a session it cannot analyse
summary: Confirmed present and unfixed, and the verifier's diagnosis holds up on inspection: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/optical_train_diagnostics_provider.dart:31-38 composes with the deprecated `ref.watch(provider.stream)`, which forwards only FUTURE events. When the Science tab has already subscribed to sessionPsfTilesProvider(id) / sessionResidualVectorsProvider(id) the source has already emitted its only value, so the derived StreamProviders never emit, psfAsync/residualsAsync stay isLoading and :65-67 returns AsyncValue.loading() forever - which is exactly why only the session the user had just viewed in Science hangs. That file is a core provider, not mine, and no change inside the Analytics screen could fix it without relocating the defect (a UI timeout would swap an indefinite skeleton for a false error).
needs_shared_change: Delete the stream re-wrapping entirely. Replace psfTilesForSessionProvider / residualVectorsForSessionProvider with plain providers that forward the AsyncValue: `final psfTilesForSessionProvider = Provider.autoDispose.family<AsyncValue<List<PsfFieldTileRow>>, int>((ref, sessionId) => ref.watch(sessionPsfTilesProvider(sessionId)));` and likewise for residuals, then drop _watchScienceRows and its `// ignore: deprecated_member_use`. opticalTrainDiagnosticsProvider already consumes AsyncValues and needs no change. Test: read sessionPsfTilesProvider(id) to completion FIRST (the Science-tab-then-Diagnostics order), then read opticalTrainDiagnosticsProvider(id) and assert it resolves to data instead of staying loading - that ordering is the whole defect, and a test that subscribes to the diagnostics provider first passes either way.

title: Exported MPC 80-column report puts the CCD observation-type code in column 14 instead of column 15
summary: Confirmed present and unfixed, and it is a two-line fix in a file I do not own: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/mpc_export_service.dart:181-185 reads `// Column 14: Note 1 - C = CCD observation` / `const note1 = 'C';` / `// Column 15: Note 2 - blank` / `const note2 = ' ';`, assembled at :225. The MPC optical-observation format puts the observation type in Note 2 (column 15); Note 1 (column 14) is a program/publication note. As shipped every record reaches the MPC with no observation type and a non-standard Note 1. The panel side (mpc_export_panel.dart) IS mine and does no formatting of its own - it only selects rows - so there is nothing to change there.
needs_shared_change: mpc_export_service.dart:181-185: `// Column 14: Note 1 - blank (program/publication note, not the observation type)` / `const note1 = ' ';` and `// Column 15: Note 2 - C = CCD observation` / `const note2 = 'C';`. The assembly at :225 already concatenates note1 then note2, so nothing else changes. Test: assert `line[13] == ' '` and `line[14] == 'C'` (0-indexed) for a formatted CCD observation, alongside the existing 80-character length check at :233.

title: Equipment readiness panel omits the mount entirely when it is disconnected
summary: Confirmed real and fully diagnosed, but every line that must change is outside my ownership list (packages/skotiq_core). The readiness report is not built on the equipment screen: readiness_provider.dart:104-112 filters camera AND mount out of offlineProfileDevices ('already covered by the critical-devices item'), while readiness_models.dart _buildCriticalDevices returns exactly ONE item for the highest-priority fault -- so `if (!cameraConnected)` returns first and the `if (!mountConnected)` branch below it is unreachable whenever both are down. With all four profile devices offline the panel names Camera, Focuser and Filter Wheel and never mentions the mount. The file I do own, screens/equipment/widgets/equipment_readiness_panel.dart, only renders the ReadinessReport; adding a mount row there would duplicate the model's authority and is precisely the 'relocate the defect' move, so I
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/readiness/readiness_models.dart, _buildCriticalDevices: make the !cameraConnected branch name the mount when it is also down. Replace that branch's const ReadinessItem with a non-const one whose detail is `mountConnected ? 'Camera is not connected. A connected camera is required before you can capture.' : 'Neither the camera nor the mount is connected. A camera is required before you can capture, and without the mount you cannot slew or track.'` and whose fixLabel is `mountConnected ? 'Connect camera' : 'Connect camera and mount'`. Leave readiness_provider.dart's filter alone (it correctly prevents double-reporting) and leave the tier assignment alone. Test: buildReadinessReport(hasProfile: true, cameraConnected: false, mountConnected: false, ...) -> the criticalDevices item's detail must contain 'mount'.

title: Red night theme renders full-saturation blue, cyan and green accent swatches
summary: Confirmed, located precisely, and found to be WORSE than reported -- but the code is in screens/settings, outside my ownership list. The swatches are packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/settings_widgets/settings_color_and_path_inputs.dart: SettingsColorPicker.accentColors (:75-83) holds exactly the hexes the reporter sampled (#5B9EC4, #10B981, #F59E0B, #EF4444, #2878A8, #EC4899, #06B6D4) and _buildColorCircle (:109) paints them raw with no reference to colors.isRedNight, mounted from screens/settings/widgets/appearance_settings.dart:70-87. The extra defect I found: resolveSkotiqThemeData (skotiq_ui/lib/src/theme/skotiq_theme.dart:43-44) returns the fixed SkotiqTheme.redNight for 'redNight' and never calls darkWithAccent/lightWithAccent -- so in red night the accent selection has NO effect on anything. The control is simultaneously a short-wavelength light
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/appearance_settings.dart, the 'Accent color' SettingRow: because red night ignores the accent entirely, replace `trailing: SettingsColorPicker(...)` with a red-night branch that renders an explanatory note instead ('Red night uses a fixed red-only palette; accent colour applies to Dark and Light.') and mirror it in the subtitle -- `settings.theme == 'redNight'` is already in scope. That removes the cyan/green/blue pixels AND stops the app offering a choice it will not honour. If a swatch row is still wanted in red night, settings_color_and_path_inputs.dart _buildColorCircle already receives SkotiqColors, so gate on colors.isRedNight and paint Color.fromARGB(255, redChannelLuminance, 0, 0) with a Tooltip carrying the option name (accentColors already stores it). Test: pump AppearanceSettings with theme 'redNight' -> find.byType(SettingsColorPicker) findsNothing; with 'dark' -> findsOneWidget.

title: Diagnostic dump is described as 'recent log files' but bundles 7 days of logs from every Skotiq instance on the machine
summary: Fixed what this screen owns; the log scoping itself lives in two packages I do not own. FIXED: (1) the save dialog no longer opens inside the application bundle -- resolveDumpSaveDirectory() now supplies an initialDirectory (Downloads, else Documents, each checked for existence) to chooseExportTarget, which previously forwarded null straight to file_selector.getSaveLocation so the picker started at the process working directory, i.e. a read-only install dir; (2) the screen scrolls, so the contents card can never clip the one button that produces a bug report. The false 'Recent log files' claim is gone, but I am explicitly NOT counting that as the fix -- I verified the export is worse than reported: LoggingService.exportLogs concatenates every file in the log dir with no time bound, and the native appender is tracing_appender::rolling::daily with NO max_log_files (bridge/src/lib.rs:337),
needs_shared_change: TWO changes, both required before the 'Recent log files' wording can honestly come back. (1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/logging_service.dart: exportLogs (:378-410) needs a bound -- e.g. exportLogs(String outputPath, {Duration? maxAge}) -- and getLogFiles (:336-365) must filter on lastModified; DiagnosticDumpService._addLogsEntry should pass ~48 h and record the actual exported span in manifest.json. Separately native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/lib.rs:337 should use the RollingFileAppender builder with .max_log_files(n) so the directory stops growing forever. (2) apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:61-68 resolves the log directory as getApplicationSupportDirectory()/logs, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR even though it SETS that variable four lines earlier; it must use the resolved data directory so two instances with different data dirs stop writing into one log file. Until (2) lands, a dump from any instance still contains every instance's capture paths and target names.

title: Sequence Library card reports 10m for a 20-frame sequence — Smart Exposure integration is dropped from the stored duration
summary: Confirmed real, and confirmed to originate entirely outside my ownership. Sequence._estimateNodeIntegration (skotiq_core sequence_state.dart, walk starts line 302) has an `if (node is ExposureNode)` branch and no SmartExposureNode branch, so Sequence.totalIntegrationSecs omits Smart Exposure; sequence_repository.dart persists (totalIntegrationSecs/60).ceil() into sequences.estimated_duration_mins, and SequenceSummary.totalIntegrationSecs is derived from that column (sequence_summary.dart:26-30). The card only renders the stored number — recomputing it in the card would need the node tree the library roll-up deliberately does not hydrate, and would leave the DB row and LongEstimatedDurationRule wrong.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart: in _estimateNodeIntegration, add a SmartExposureNode branch beside the ExposureNode one — SequenceEstimate(estimatedSecs: node.totalIntegrationSecs, singleIterationSecs: node.totalIntegrationSecs, isUnbounded: node.loopUntilStopped) (loopUntilStopped has no bounded integration: either mark unbounded or use integrationBudgetSecs when > 0). Existing rows keep their stale estimate until re-saved, so a recompute-on-load or migration is worth considering. LongEstimatedDurationRule (settings_rules.dart:157) reads the same stored value; the finding's claim that the disk-space rule also reads it is wrong (verifier confirmed disk_space_rules.dart has no such reference).
